description: An ex-offender's feel-good economy rice stall in Woodlands where you pile over 20 dishes onto one plate for a flat S$7 — no refills, but no limits on what or how much you take. Dishes rotate with fresh options like chilli crab and Peranakan specials, plus a salmon dish that sold out on debut. Run by two veteran chefs who keep prices low through supplier relationships.
parking: Public parking around the Woodlands Ave 12 industrial estate
title: R&B Cai Fan — $7 all-you-can-pile buffet cai fan
why: New Jun 2026 opening; unbeatable value lunch in the north

description: Chef Antonio Miscellaneo's crowd-favourite Italian concept opened its first East outlet at Tampines Mall, bringing its popular Newpolitan pizzas and pastas eastward. Six dishes are exclusive to this outlet — including the smoked Margherita Affumicata ($19), Prosciutto e Nduja pizza ($24), and seabass-stuffed Agnolotti al Branzino e Gamberi ($27) — all under $30. Walk-ins only; expect the brand's signature snaking queues.
title: Casa Vostra — casual Italian lands in Tampines
why: New May 2026 opening; first Casa Vostra in the East with exclusive dishes

description: The weekend alter-ego of hawker bakery Cat in the Hat, where self-taught baker Jesper Chan bakes naturally-leavened breads fermented with fruit yeast waters. Standouts include the Apple Yeast Water Rye Shokupan ($6), Red Wine Baguette with cranberry, walnut and cream cheese ($4), and a Sourdough Ebi Katsu Sando ($5). It routinely sells out — go early, because when the trays are empty by 3pm, that's it till next weekend.
title: Wild Honey Pie — weekend-only sourdough bakery
why: Weekend-only concept — only chance to go this week is Sat-Sun

address: 1 Jurong West Central 2, #01-33, Jurong Point JP1, Singapore 648886
description: The Texas wing chain has returned to Jurong Point with a larger dine-in space decked out in its signature emerald green, graphic banners and neon lights. Order the classics — boneless wings from $11.30 for six, classic wings from $11.80 — in any of 12 seasonings, or try the two Jurong-exclusive sides: hand-cut onion rings ($6.45) and Cajun fried corn ($6.45).
title: Wingstop — bigger Jurong Point comeback
why: Reopened bigger in May 2026 with Jurong-exclusive sides

description: Yishun's park-facing hawker centre changed hands on 20 Jul 2026, with Canopy Hawkers Group (which also runs Canberra Hawker Centre) taking over management and promising fresh ideas and a more vibrant experience. Expect the usual north-side favourites alongside new stalls, plus budget-friendly options across the board. Open daily 6am-10pm, so it covers breakfast through supper.
parking: Two floors of carpark above the hawker centre
title: Yishun Park Hawker Centre — new operator, fresh buzz
why: New operator since Jul 2026 — worth a fresh look this week

description: Singapore's largest integrated community hub celebrates its 2nd anniversary with a week of free school-holiday activities — bouncy castles, inflatable play zones, kiddy rides, tabletop games and arts-and-crafts workshops. The celebrations peak on Sun 13 Sep with the Birthday Bash carnival (interactive games, gachapon prizes, old-school photo booth) and a Mid-Autumn light-up with lantern displays, cultural performances and crafts from 6pm to 10pm.
title: One Punggol 2nd Birthday Bash — carnival + Mid-Autumn light-up
when: Sun 13 Sep; bash daytime, Mid-Autumn light-up 6pm-10pm
why: One-day-only birthday bash + Mid-Autumn celebration, 13 Sep

description: Gardens by the Bay's Mid-Autumn Festival lantern display opens Saturday 12 September 2026, running 6pm–10pm daily through 27 September. Large-scale illuminated lantern sets spread across Supertree Grove, Golden Garden and Bayfront Plaza, with a marketplace, carnival games and a Colonnade of 1,000 hand-painted lanterns. The LED Lion Dance launches the festival on 12 September at 8.30pm. Outdoor grounds are free to enter.
parking: Car parks at Bayfront Plaza and The Meadow; nearest MRT is Bayfront (CE1/DT16)
price: Free (workshop fees and Flower Dome tickets apply separately)
title: Mid-Autumn Festival Lanterns @ Gardens by the Bay — opening-night lantern wonderland
why: It opens on Saturday night of this week — opening night has the LED Lion Dance at 8.30pm

description: Gardens by the Bay's first Egyptian-themed floral display fills the Flower Dome with more than 7,000 lilies across 46 species, including the Egyptian blue waterlily and giant Victoria waterlilies. A 4.5-metre Abu Simbel-style facade, painted temple columns and deity statues frame a central Nile-inspired pond. The display runs through 27 September 2026, daily 9am–9pm; Flower Dome admission applies.
parking: Car parks at Bayfront Plaza and The Meadow; nearest MRT is Bayfront (CE1/DT16)
title: Lilytopia — Egyptian-themed floral display in the Flower Dome
why: Timed display in its final two weeks — pair with the Mid-Autumn lanterns next door at night

description: NParks runs a free guided tour of Sungei Buloh Wetland Reserve every Saturday from 9.30am to 11.30am, led by experienced volunteer guides through the mangrove and freshwater wetland trails. Expect migratory birds, mudskippers, horseshoe crabs and monitor lizards. Maximum 15 participants and online registration is required; walks are cancelled if it rains.
parking: On-site parking at the Visitor Centre; registration is via nparks.gov.sg and closes when the 15 slots fill
title: Sungei Buloh free guided walk — Saturday morning mangrove nature tour
why: The only scheduled Saturday guided walk this week — free and family-friendly

description: Singapore's only daily night show staged outdoors over the open sea at Siloso Beach, telling the story of Shahbaz the mythical bird with 3D water-screen projections, lasers, fountains, fire and a fireworks finale. Two shows nightly at 7.40pm and 8.40pm, each about 20 minutes. Standard tickets start from S$22; September deals on sentosa.com.sg offer $12 tickets for locals.
parking: Beach Station Car Park; easiest by Sentosa Express to Beach Station
price: ~$22 standard ticket ($12 locals promo in Sep)
title: Wings of Time — nightly fireworks show over the sea at Sentosa
why: Singapore's only daily fireworks show — reliable nightly anchor for any evening plan
